finding.claim: GET /users has no authentication or authorization check, and the org filter comes straight from the query string. Any caller can list the id and name of every user in any organization by changing ?org=. This is a cross-tenant IDOR. It is only exploitable if no upstream middleware, such as a gateway or auth layer that also populates req.pg, enforces access. No such middleware appears in this file. Confidence is moderate.
finding.source: req.query.org (attacker-chosen org identifier, unauthenticated HTTP request)
finding.sink: req.pg.query("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1") with the result returned via res.json(rows)

trace.note: The express app is created and no auth or session middleware is registered with app.use.
The /users handler is registered with no per-route authorization.
req.query.org is passed unchanged as the org filter. The query is parameterized, so there is no SQL injection, but the value is never compared to the caller's own org.
The rows for the requested org are returned to the caller.

finding.guards_checked: The query is parameterized ($1), so there is no SQL injection. I found no authentication middleware, no check tying org to the caller's identity, and no rate limiting in this file. req.pg is never set here, so it must come from external middleware that was not visible. Other routes were checked and found safe. /file resolves the path and enforces a ROOT+path.sep prefix check, so there is no traversal. /count calls execFile with a fixed argv, so there is no command injection.

verdict.guard_found: none (only parameterization at db.js:9, which stops SQL injection but not cross-tenant access)
verdict.reason: db.js:8-10 passes the unauthenticated req.query.org into the users query and returns the rows, and the whole project has no app.use or auth check (db.js:5, app.listen at :23); the caveat is that req.pg is never set in the code, so the route only works if an external layer supplies it, and that layer is not visible.

verdict_facts.guard_found: none (the query is parameterized at db.js:9, which blocks SQLi but not IDOR; no auth, role or org-ownership check in this file)
verdict_facts.reason: db.js:8-10 passes the attacker-supplied req.query.org straight into the users query and returns the rows with no comparison to the caller's identity or org, so any HTTP client can read any tenant's users. The only caveat is that unseen upstream middleware could scope req.pg, e.g. with row-level security, but the project facts only say it populates identity, not that it enforces access.
